title: Multi-spot hedged GPU fallback routing with budget windows and graceful model fallbacks
creator: Asha Patel
description: Problem: We need to improve cost efficiency and robustness of inference routing when operating across heterogeneous cloud spot pools and on-demand capacity while preserving SLOs. Current single-path spot fallback triggers frequently during transient capacity pressure and causes oscillation and higher tail latency. Goal: Implement a hedged multi-spot routing strategy that bids requests across prioritized spot pools and GPU classes within a short hedging window, enforce per-customer and per-route budget windows (soft caps + emergency headroom), and support graceful model-variant fallbacks (quantized/trimmed variants) when capacity or budget constraints exceed thresholds.
background: Customers use Dedicated and Hosted deployments with mixed spot/on-demand capacity. We already have budget caps and region tiering work, but traffic spikes and spot evictions cause costly on-demand fallbacks and degraded latencies. Research shows small hedged retries across diverse spot pools can reduce tail latency and eviction cost without always hitting expensive on-demand. Additionally, model-variant fallbacks (lower-precision or shorter-context variants) can reduce GPU needs while keeping outputs acceptable for some routes.
acceptance_criteria: Routing layer can attempt up to N hedged requests across distinct spot pools within configurable hedging_ms (default 40ms)
Per-customer and per-route soft budget windows are enforced with graceful throttling before hard caps are applied
Fallback chain supports model variants: full-precision -> quantized INT8 -> truncated-context variant -> on-demand fallback
Unit and integration tests cover hedging logic, budget window transitions, and fallback ordering
Metrics dashboards show spend delta, hedged success rate, latency tail (p95/p99) improvement, and on-demand spill decrease by at least 15% in canary traffic
technical_notes: Design: 1) Hedging controller: at request arrival evaluate candidate pools (region, GPU class, spot stability score, remaining budget). 2) Create hedged proposals and issue parallel warm-start requests to 2-3 pools depending on priority. 3) First successful stream wins; cancel the others to minimize double-charge risk (use a cancellation token and best-effort cancel RPC). 4) Budget windows: implement sliding-window soft caps (e.g., spend_ms / spend_tokens) per-customer and per-route with token-bucket refill and emergency headroom reserve. 5) Fallback profiles: attach policy chains to routes mapping to model variants by cost and latency characteristics. 6) Telemetry: trace hedging decisions, pool-health signals, and budget transitions for observability. Trade-offs: hedging increases transient compute usage; must be limited by budget windows and backpressure. Cancellation is best-effort and some double billing is possible; plan for accounting reconciliation and dashboarding.
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (2 weeks): Implement hedging controller prototype in routing service; unit tests; canary with internal accounts in us-east-1 only
Phase 2 (3 weeks): Add budget window enforcement hooks and per-route policy config; integrate model-variant lookup; e2e tests and chaos testing (simulate spot eviction)
Phase 3 (2 weeks): Observability dashboards, cost reconciliation job, automated rollback guard, and broader canary across regions
Phase 4 (1 week): Docs, console UI flags for canary opt-in, and runbook updates
rollout_plan: Start with 10% of internal traffic routed through hedging in us-east-1; monitor cost and p99. Gradually expand to 1% external customers (opt-in) after stable results; then 25% across low-risk enterprise accounts. Enable model-variant fallbacks only after users opt-in or route explicitly allows fallbacks. Final global rollout contingent on on-demand spill reduction and <=2% increase in total token billing due to hedging during learning period.
test_plan: Automated unit tests for hedging decisions; integration tests that mock multiple pool latencies and evictions; chaos test injecting spot evictions and network partitions; billing simulation to measure double-charge risk; canary monitoring with alerting on cost delta, p99 regressions, and hedged success anomalies.
metrics: hedged_success_rate: ratio of requests served by a hedged spot before spilling to on-demand
on_demand_spill_rate: percent of requests routed to on-demand after hedging and fallbacks
cost_delta_vs_baseline: percent change in compute spend for canary cohort
p95_latency_ms and p99_latency_ms for routes with hedging enabled
risks: Hedging may cause temporary spikes in GPU allocations and increase short-term spend; mitigations: strict hedging_ms and budget windows
Cancellation is best-effort leading to potential double charges; mitigations: reconcile billing and apply crediting rules for hedged duplicates
Model-variant fallbacks may degrade output quality for some routes; mitigation: require route-level opt-in and add A/B eval hooks
open_questions: Optimal default hedging_ms that balances tail reduction vs duplicate cost (40ms is tentative)
How to score spot pool stability across cloud providers in a portable way? (historical eviction rate vs real-time telemetry)
Should hedging be limited to specific GPU classes (A100, H100) or include cheaper GPU types with slower throughput?
